allowed_claims: The attribution to L. Peter Deutsch

hooks.hook_text: A published University of Toronto CSC236 Summer 2025 schedule places Recursive Algorithms in Lectures 5 and 6 and Recursive Correctness in Lecture 7.
allowed_claims: Recursive Algorithms appears in Lectures 5 and 6 on that published schedule
Recursive Correctness appears in Lecture 7 on that published schedule

hooks.hook_text: On December 31, 2008, 30GB Zune players froze because a leap-year date routine could repeat a while-loop iteration without changing the state needed to exit.
allowed_claims: The affected product was the 30GB Zune
The leap-year branch could leave the loop state unchanged and keep the loop running
hooks.verification_level: contemporaneous technical report with code excerpt

internal_style_seeds.seed: Use the classic self-referential programmer joke: 'To understand recursion, first understand recursion.' Do not attribute it to a person. Turn the circularity into a question about why a correctness proof needs independently justified smaller calls.
Challenge the belief that returning the right-looking value on tested inputs is enough for correctness; the reading also requires normal termination and the postcondition.
Map a finite recursive call tree to a familiar process with a measurable resource that strictly decreases at each step. Preserve the distinction between valid calls and eventual termination.
Make the student a code reviewer deciding whether a proposed recursive-correctness argument proves both valid recursive calls and a finite call tree.
